Step 1: Fact: Anne is young.  
Step 2: By rule “All young things are quiet” and fact “Anne is young,” derive “Anne is quiet.”  
Step 3: By rule “If something is quiet then it is smart” and “Anne is quiet,” derive “Anne is smart.”  
Step 4: By rule “Smart things are nice” and “Anne is smart,” derive “Anne is nice.”  
Step 5: By rule “All nice things are furry” and “Anne is nice,” derive “Anne is furry.”  
Step 6: By rule “Furry things are not red” and “Anne is furry,” derive “Anne is not red.”

Rejected step: To use “If something is smart and not rough then it is red” to derive “Anne is red,” we would need “Anne is smart” and “Anne is not rough.” “Anne is smart” is derived, but “Anne is not rough” is not given or derived; the facts state “Anne is rough.” Therefore this rule cannot license “Anne is red.”

No other rule derives “Anne is red,” while “Anne is not red” is derived.

ANSWER: False
